learning system call filtering policies automatically for microservices operating in a containerized environment. At runtime, the system learns the authorized system calls allowed for an application while rejecting attempts to invoke any unauthorized (spurious) calls. This is particularly significant given the continuing evolution of security strategies that rely on strict process isolation via individual containers; despite this architecture, vulnerabilities such as those exploiting kernel-level flaws remain actionable. By aggregating multiple services, microservices environments inherently interact with the shared operating system, thereby expanding the potential attack surface.

Motivated by these challenges, our goal was to create a generic system for system-call-level protection. Timeloops achieves this by utilizing machine learning to identify patterns in an application's legitimate system-call sequences. The solution is designed for simplicity and efficiency, implementing the filtering layer as a lightweight loop integrated within the software package. Tipping the scale at merely 15 KB, the system demonstrates remarkable versatility. Validated across various workloads including single-worker applications, database systems, web servers, and multi-shielded microservices clusters, Timeloops successfully blocks malicious invocation attempts, such as those from a container running a MongoDB microservice, without impairing the host's performance. Source code and images are accessible at https://github.com/pcap/Timeloops.

a strong geodetic set is defined as a vertex set \( S \subseteq V(G) \) that allows covering all nodes within \(V(G) \setminus S\) by utilizing unique shortest paths between every distinct vertex pair within \( S \).
